title: War of Geniuses: Walk Out of the Checks
summary: Use a bishop sacrifice to escape repeated rook checks, then preserve a mating pattern instead of collecting the rook too early.

nodes.question: How can White answer the rook check and keep the pawn alive?
nodes.explanation: After ...Ra6+, White has Ka1/Bc1/Nf5/f7 against Kh8/Bc8/Ra6. White must answer check without losing the promotion threat.

nodes.question: Should White accept the rook on g4?
nodes.explanation: The king has reached g5, but ...Rg4+ offers the rook with a bishop-fork resource.

nodes.question: How can White defeat the final rook blockade?
nodes.explanation: White Kh6/Nf5/f7 faces Kh8/Bc8/Rg8. Promoting by capture immediately lets the king recapture; improving the knight changes the mating geometry.

branches.title: Sacrifice, walk, and finish with a knight mate
commentary: After ...Ra6+, White has Ka1/Bc1/Nf5/f7 against Kh8/Bc8/Ra6. White must answer check without losing the promotion threat.
Ba3 blocks the a-file check. Giving up the bishop lets the king emerge without allowing the rook to return to f6.
Rxa3+ accepts the bishop and renews the a-file check.
Kb2 steps off the file. The rook on a3 cannot now return directly to f6.
Ra2+ sacrifices the rook: taking it allows the bishop fork on e6.
Kc1 declines the rook and begins the king walk.
Ra1+ follows with another rank check.
Kd2 leaves the first rank while keeping the pawn threat.
Ra2+ continues checking along the second rank.
Ke3 climbs off that rank. The source illustrates this selected checking route.
Ra3+ checks along the third rank.
Kf4 continues toward the knight’s shelter.
Ra4+ follows onto the fourth rank.
Kg5 reaches the kingside, but Black still has a final sacrifice.
Rg4+ offers the rook directly to the king. The plus sign matters: this move is check.
Kh6 declines the rook and keeps the king advanced.
Rg8 blocks the pawn’s capture-promotion route by offering a king recapture. This is the illustrated final defense.
Ne7 improves the knight before promoting. The knight can deliver mate on g6 if Black’s bishop is drawn onto g8.
Be6 covers f7 and supports g8. This is the source’s selected bishop defense.
fxg8=Q+ captures the rook with check and offers the new queen to the bishop.
Bxg8 captures the queen but occupies the king’s flight square on g8.
Ng6# is mate. Kh6 covers g7/h7, the knight checks h8, and Black’s own bishop blocks g8.
branches.explanation: Ng6# is mate. Kh6 covers g7/h7, the knight checks h8, and Black’s own bishop blocks g8.

branches.title: The direct king exit lets the rook return
commentary: After ...Ra6+, White has Ka1/Bc1/Nf5/f7 against Kh8/Bc8/Ra6. White must answer check without losing the promotion threat.
Kb2 exits check but gives up the exact win. The bishop is still on c1 instead of having diverted the rook.
Rf6 returns behind the pawn and stops promotion. The exact position is drawn with best play; “losing the advantage” is not the same as a forced loss.
branches.explanation: Rf6 returns behind the pawn and stops promotion. The exact position is drawn with best play; “losing the advantage” is not the same as a forced loss.

branches.title: Taking the first rook offer allows a fork
commentary: After ...Ra6+, White has Ka1/Bc1/Nf5/f7 against Kh8/Bc8/Ra6. White must answer check without losing the promotion threat.
Ba3 diverts the rook.
Rxa3+ takes the bishop with check.
Kb2 escapes the file.
Ra2+ offers the rook while preparing a bishop fork.
Kxa2 accepts the rook, but abandons the forced win.
Be6+ checks the king on a2 and attacks the pawn on f7.
Kb2 answers the check.
Bxf7 removes the pawn. Knight versus bishop with the kings is an exact draw here.
branches.explanation: Bxf7 removes the pawn. Knight versus bishop with the kings is an exact draw here.

branches.title: Taking on g4 gives a drawn pawn ending
commentary: White is in check from Rg4. Compare capturing it with the winning Kh6.
Kxg4 collects the rook but gives up the exact win.
Bxf5+ captures the knight with check and offers a second liquidation.
Kxf5 recaptures the bishop, leaving only the f-pawn and kings.
Kg7 heads toward the pawn’s stopping square.
Ke6 advances with the pawn, but cannot force promotion against this defense.
Kf8 blocks the pawn. The exact pawn ending is drawn; Black has survived by giving away the rook.
branches.explanation: Kf8 blocks the pawn. The exact pawn ending is drawn; Black has survived by giving away the rook.

branches.title: After the king advances, decline the bishop recapture
commentary: The rook capture is different after White improves the king from g5 to h6.
Kh6 preserves the win instead of accepting the rook on g4.
Rg6+ is the source’s alternative rook offer.
Kxg6 takes it with the king already advanced.
Bxf5+ again captures the knight, but now White need not take the bishop.
Kf6 leaves the bishop on the board and supports f7’s promotion. The exact ending remains winning for White.
branches.explanation: Kf6 leaves the bishop on the board and supports f7’s promotion. The exact ending remains winning for White.

branches.title: Promote before improving the knight
commentary: The rook on g8 can be captured, but the knight has not yet reached the mating setup.
fxg8=Q+ gives up the forced win. Black can use the king to capture the queen.
Kxg8 removes the queen. The remaining knight versus bishop position is drawn; Ne7 first changes which piece can recapture and supplies the mating jump.
branches.explanation: Kxg8 removes the queen. The remaining knight versus bishop position is drawn; Ne7 first changes which piece can recapture and supplies the mating jump.

exercises.prompt: Why does capturing the rook on g4 fail?
exercises.answer: Black can remove the knight with check and reach a drawn king-and-pawn ending. Advancing to h6 first changes the liquidation.
The knight gains g6. After the bishop is drawn onto g8, Ng6 is mate because Black’s bishop occupies its own king’s only remaining flight square.

startContext: Begin after ...Ra6+ at 14s, a complete seven-piece diagram reconstructed from the saved board. The main selected checking route, early and late rook sacrifices, final knight preparation, and immediate capture-promotion error are checked throughout. The lines illustrate selected defenses rather than an exhaustive legal-move tree. Exact draws are described as draws even when the narration loosely says the advantage is lost.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
